headline: Monitor Local Signage for Storm Impact and Road Access
reservation: Entry to the forest areas does not typically require a formal reservation system, but visitors must check current status for storm damage. Access is via single-track roads which are strictly unsuitable for coaches; verify current land management notices before travel.

days.title: Riverside Trails and Pine Forests

stops.name: Dog Falls
stops.detail: Walk to the dark pools and rushing rapids, then continue to the pine trees by Coire Loch or climb to a viewpoint overlooking the glen.

days.driving: Allow 30-40 minutes; conditions on single-track roads vary
days.note: Follow all local signage regarding storm-affected areas and turn back if paths appear unsafe.

intel.title: Single Track Restrictions
intel.text: Approaches to the glen consist of narrow single-track roads that are not suitable for large coaches. Drivers should be prepared to use passing places and monitor local conditions.

intel.title: Storm Recovery Updates
intel.text: Forestry and Land Scotland monitors storm impact continuously, so website data may lag behind reality. Always prioritize on-site signage over digital guides.

intel.title: Site Parking Information
intel.text: Evidence does not specify parking capacity or fee structures for the Dog Falls area. Visitors should arrive with a backup plan if designated areas are full.

intel.title: Connectivity Gaps
intel.text: The evidence does not provide details on mobile signal strength within the glen. It is advisable to download maps for offline use before leaving gateway towns.

intel.title: Supply and Fuel Availability
intel.text: Specific fuel locations within Glen Affric are not documented in official sources. Ensure the vehicle is sufficiently fueled in Cannich or Inverness before entering the glen.

plan.arrival: Pick up supplies in Inverness or Cannich before navigating the single-track approach to the forest trailheads.
plan.vehicle: Standard cars are suitable, but large coaches are prohibited on the approach roads.
plan.goldenHour: The viewpoint up the glen offers elevated perspectives for sunset, though visibility depends on local Highland weather.
